rationale: A number written in a national format carries no country code, so it can only be recognized against a region. With the region set to GB, a UK national-format number is phone data and must be detected.
This is the whole point of the region property: without it the same text is unrecognizable as a phone number.
The same UK national-format number under the default region produces no span. A national format is only meaningful relative to a region, and this one is not a valid number in the default region.
Paired with region-gb-national-format, this pins that the region property is what changes the outcome rather than the number being detected regardless.
A '+'-prefixed number carries its own country code, so it is unambiguous without a region and must be detected whatever the region is set to.
Configured here as GB against a US number, so a region setting that suppressed out-of-region international numbers would fail.
